newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin welcomes results of Chechen election.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin welcomes results of Chechen election.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday welcomed the preliminary result of Chechnya's presidential election, which point to victory for moderate Aslan Maskhadov, saying it would help keep peace talks on track.

"The preliminary results of the voting, in the president's opinion, give a serious chance for productive negotiations to continue between the federal government and the new Chechen leadership," Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.

"The result (of these negotiations) will be the mutually acceptable resolution of all questions defining the status of the Chechen republic within the Russian Federation," said Yastrzhembsky, making clear the Kremlin still rules out full independence for the breakaway region.

Maskhadov, the rebel military chief who also led the Chechen delegation in last summer's peace talks with Moscow, is a staunch supporter of Chechen independence but has made clear he will seek better relations with Russia if elected president.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin, who is recovering from double pneumonia, had discussed the Chechen elections with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during a short working visit to the Kremlin earlier on Tuesday.

Yeltsin has admitted his decision to send troops into Chechnya in December 1994 to crush the mainly Moslem region's independence bid was one of his biggest political mistakes. Tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, died during 21 months of fighting that ended with last August's peace deal.
